Allon-bachuth
AL-on-BAK-uth
proper noun
Hebrew 'Allon bakuth, “the oak of weeping,” from 'allon, an oak or great tree, and bakah, to weep; the tree beneath Bethel where Deborah, Rebekah’s nurse, was buried.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

📖 Biblical Definition

Even the tears of a servant are named and remembered in the book of God. Beneath Bethel, under an oak, they buried Deborah, Rebekah’s nurse, “and the name of it was called Allonbachuth” (Gen 35:8), the oak of weeping. She was no princess, no prophet—a nurse, an old woman who had carried Rebekah from Padan-aram—yet her death drew the household of Jacob to honest grief, and the place kept the memory of their weeping. Scripture does not despise the sorrow of the saints nor hurry them past the grave with a hollow cheer. It sanctifies their tears, giving the very tree a name that means weeping. Yet the oak of weeping stands hard by Bethel, the house of God, where Jacob had seen the ladder set up to heaven; and so the grief is hedged about with covenant. Those who pass through the valley of Baca, the vale of weeping, make it a well (Psa 84:6), for godly sorrow springs into hope. The LORD leads His mourners beside the still waters (Psa 23:2) and renews the strength of them that wait upon Him, that they may mount up with wings as eagles (Isa 40:31). Allon-bachuth teaches us to weep without despair. We sorrow, but not as others which have no hope; the dust of the faithful, like Deborah’s, rests under the shadow of the house of God, awaiting the morning when death itself shall be swallowed up in victory.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

“The oak of weeping” beneath Bethel where Deborah, Rebekah’s nurse, was buried (Gen 35:8); a witness to the sanctified sorrow of God’s people and the hope beyond the grave.

expand to see more

ALLON-BACHUTH, the oak of weeping beneath Bethel (Gen 35:8).

There Deborah, Rebekah’s nurse, was buried.

The household of Jacob mourned an old and faithful servant.

The very tree kept the memory of their weeping.

A witness that God sanctifies the tears of His saints.

📖 Key Scripture

Gen 35:8 — "But Deborah Rebekah's nurse died, and she was buried beneath Bethel under an oak: and the name of it was called Allonbachuth."

Psa 84:6 — "Who passing through the valley of Baca make it a well; the rain also filleth the pools."

Psa 23:2 — "He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters."

Isa 40:31 — "But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Allon-bachuth recovers the godly sorrow of the saints—tears named and remembered, yet hedged about with covenant hope.

expand to see more

The oak of weeping stands hard by Bethel, the house of God, and there the household of Jacob buried an old and faithful nurse with honest grief. Scripture does not hurry the saints past the grave with a hollow cheer, but sanctifies their tears, giving the very tree a name that means weeping.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. An oak beneath Bethel stirs no modern controversy. The principle to recover is the godly sorrow of the saints, tears named and remembered, yet hedged about with covenant hope. We sorrow, but not as others which have no hope; those who pass through the vale of weeping make it a well, for the faithful dead rest under the shadow of the house of God.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From 'allon, an oak or great tree, and bakah, to weep; “the oak of weeping.”

expand to see more

'Allon bakuth — the oak of weeping (Gen 35:8).

'allon — an oak or sturdy tree.

bakah — to weep, bewail, lament.

The same root sounds in the valley of Baca, the vale of weeping.

The tree stood near Bethel, the house of God.

Usage

"They buried Deborah under the oak called Allon-bachuth."

"Allon-bachuth means the oak of weeping."

"The place kept the memory of the mourning of Jacob’s house."
